subject: WO-8 round 5c: creation-time canonical identity for live checkouts; review-lane flake diagnosed and guarded

seed.consequence: The trappable-signal handler now re-raises the fatal signal before it sweeps, so the process is terminated with the cleanup call still unexecuted and every interrupted run leaves its live writable checkout directory and a stale git worktree registration behind in the repository under examination.
seed.rationale: MAJOR: incorrect behavior reachable by ordinary use (any Ctrl+C / console-close during a verification run) and a violation of the order the surrounding comment states explicitly ('Sweep, then re-raise the signal'), reintroducing the leak that handler exists to prevent; it is not CRITICAL because nothing is corrupted and no gate or verdict is silently wrong -- the leftovers are reclaimed by the next run's startup sweep.
hazard_terms: cleanup sequenced after the call that ends the process
teardown that never runs on the abort path
resource left behind on an interrupt path

suite_at_variant: tests/verifier.test.js: "98 passed, 0 failed"; tests/review-lane.test.js: "OK — 114 passed, 0 failed"
design_note: Reordering a signal handler to 'drop our listener, re-raise, then clean up' is a natural-looking tidy-up and the sort of edit a lifetime-focused change invites, but a re-raised SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGBREAK takes its default action immediately, so the trailing sweep is dead code and the 'exit' listener never fires either. No suite sends a signal to a process that holds a live checkout -- review-lane exercises the review runner's own scratch teardown, not this module's -- so both suites stay green while a probe (emit the signal after creating a checkout) shows the base commit leaving the worktree list clean and the variant leaving both the directory and the registration behind.
